notes:
Inbound SMB lead. CTO (Priya) and lead engineer (Jamal) building an in-app assistant for their low-code IDE. Primary ask: hosted API, easy self-serve to get to Prod with predictable costs.

They ran quick experiments against a 13B Llama variant (community) and a Mistral-mini; observed noticeable quality gap on code-assistant prompts (refactor/intent extraction). Quote from call: "We need helpful, not hallucination-prone — but can't afford full 70B runs yet."

Main questions raised during discovery:
- Llama vs Mistral vs Qwen: where is the pragmatic sweet spot for dev-assistant tasks?
- Cost tradeoffs: quantized 4-bit models vs higher-quality fp16 variants — which will reduce token spend without degrading completion quality?
- Latency targets: aiming p95 < 300ms for short-turn chat (<= 200 tokens) to keep UI feeling snappy; currently seeing p95 ~ 420ms on community endpoints.
- Embeddings: test showed Mistral-embed >= cosine similarity for doc search, but cost per embedding is key (50k monthly embeddings).

Security: need SSO (SAML) and audit logs for admin dashboard; SOC2 preferred but not blocked if roadmap and attestation planned. Data residency: US only for now.

Operational constraints: small engineering team; wants minimal infra ops. Prefers hosted API (self-serve) with predictable throttles/quotas and simple SDK. Interested in Redwood's Optimize suggestions if they can save >20% monthly spend.

Actionables from AE/SE:
- Prepare a 1-page model selection matrix (quality vs cost vs latency) comparing: Llama-13B quantized, Mistral-7B fp16, Qwen-7B-mid, and Redwood-curated 13B variant. Include expected token cost per 1k tokens and estimated p95 on hosted API.
- Provide quickstart snippet for embeddings + small batching example showing cost diff.
- Book them into a Wed office hours slot for live walk-through.

Stated internal priority: pilot in Q2, goal to ship MVP assistant to beta customers in Q3.

Notes style: shorthand, bullet fragments, call references. See linked drive doc for raw prompt tests and transcript (ff_20260303).
